_note: How an answer in English is compared (see sl.json for the fields). same: a contraction is the same answer as its long form (don't = do not, I'm = I am, it's = it is, can't = cannot; he's got = he has got: 's before got is has, so it comes first; Jack's at home = Jack is at home, only before a word a possessive never stands before: an article, not, a preposition of place, here, there, a possessive, always, never, very; I'd like = I would like); a number from 21 to 99 with or without its hyphen (twenty-one, twenty one); a hundred and five as the American a hundred five; the American spelling as the British (color = colour, favorite = favourite, center = centre, meter = metre, gray = grey, mom = mum, traveling = travelling, pajamas = pyjamas, plow = plough, math = maths, dialog = dialogue, program = programme), and -ize and -ise both British (realise, realize). No letters to fold. wrong: the plural's known mistakes, each only for a noun of its group, never a slip of the keyboard on another noun: -s for -es after x, z, ch, sh, ss (boxs for boxes, churchs for churches, glasss for glasses) and buss for buses; -fes for -ves on the nouns that make it (knifes, wifes, lifes, calfes for knives, wives, lives, calves; gloves and loves keep their slips); woman for women and women for woman (one letter apart, else forgiven as a slip; man and men are too short for one); the numbers' spelling mistakes (fourty for forty, forteen for fourteen, ninty for ninety, ninteen for nineteen, for for four), which a slip in the stem would forgive.
